title: fix(sqlite): preserve final worker diagnostics during close
body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite workers can lose their final diagnostic lines when the last backend closes and the broker immediately terminates the worker.

## User Impact

Graceful final-backend close gives pending console output a bounded chance to reach stdout/stderr before acknowledging completion, including when another open is queued. The existing five-second fallback makes this best effort. Database cleanup, queued-write settlement, and error/forced retirement retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

SQLite replies and Node worker stdio use separate message channels, so a successful close reply does not prove buffered diagnostics were delivered. Drain output after backend and delegation cleanup but before the successful final-actor close reply.

The existing output-drain helper moves to `src/process`; CLI exit, native-hook relay, and sealed-worker error callers move with it. Its callback behavior and timeout stay unchanged, and the old path is removed without an alias. The existing real-worker logging fixture gains a bounded teardown burst while preserving its exact JSON and terminal-diagnostic assertions.

## Evidence

- The [original Linux / Node 24.19 CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35169490650/job/105038182508), observed while validating #150399, had valid JSON output and open/execute diagnostics but no terminal close diagnostic. The affected logging owners were unchanged by that PR.
- On macOS / Node 24.19, a pure-Node close-burst probe lost the final line in **31/32** ACK-then-terminate trials, with up to 3,879 stderr bytes still queued at the ACK. Waiting for the write callback lost **0/32**. The simple three-line probe and original unmodified test passed locally; those results are retained separately.
- The strengthened **existing SQLite-worker test failed before the production fix** with only the first teardown diagnostic delivered, then passed after it. **156 focused tests passed** across logging, SQLite lifecycle/store behavior, runtime guards, sealed-worker entry, and one-shot CLI output, including callback/fallback and real piped JSON/TTY checks. The logging regression passed again on final syntax.
- Deslop, final independent P2 review, targeted typed lint, core types, and the remaining selected schema, database, media, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook, and auth guards passed. Full tracked-source search found no old helper-path or symbol references.

The initial `check:changed` run passed its preceding guards, production/test typechecks, and export scans, then rejected an implicit-return Promise executor. That expression now uses the equivalent block body. Final targeted typed lint, the logging test, incremental core types, and the exact remaining guards passed; the original aggregate failure is retained rather than relabeled green. The full test suite was not run locally. The [first PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35174320069/job/105052733677) passed the real SQLite logging regression on Linux, including the terminal close diagnostic, with 563 passing and two skipped tests in its storage/runtime shard. That run remained red on unrelated Control UI, Qwen, preparation-fixture, and compiler-tooling checks.

The refreshed head includes the landed Control UI, Qwen, and preparation-fixture fixes. Its SQLite patch is byte-identical to the reviewed patch, and all ten accepted source-file hashes are unchanged. [Required CI completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35180012533) for this exact head. Its first attempt cancelled two jobs before runner acquisition; the approved failed-only rerun completed both Node test shards on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu. The canonical watcher reports green and the exact run receipt confirms attempt 2 succeeded. Prior failures remain retained, and no test timeout or assertion was relaxed.
